props.name: The activity of a freshly reduced catalyst rises with use to a maximum and then
props.statement: The activity of a freshly reduced catalyst rises with use to a maximum and then falls, the fall being sharper than the rise; 5 % excess hydrogen instantly checks the fall.

props.name: Over a further period of about 14 hours even 5 % hydrogen did not prevent the ac
props.statement: Over a further period of about 14 hours even 5 % hydrogen did not prevent the activity from falling; changing to 10 % gave a slight but definite rise, but the tendency to fall was not overcome.

props.name: Treatment with hydrogen partially revivified the catalyst (originally 80 % activ
props.statement: Treatment with hydrogen partially revivified the catalyst (originally 80 % activity when freshly prepared); hydrogen is removed from the surface with difficulty and activity rises progressively as it is removed.

props.name: Although thermodynamically possible, formaldehyde as intermediate in the methano
props.statement: Although thermodynamically possible, formaldehyde as intermediate in the methanol synthesis is considered unlikely, given its marked tendency to polymerise under hydrogen pressure rather than be reduced, and the preferential chemisorption of CO.

props.name: The water and CO2 evolved when the high-chromium catalyst was flushed with nitro
props.statement: The water and CO2 evolved when the high-chromium catalyst was flushed with nitrogen at 450 °C can be explained only by further reduction of the chromium oxide by chemisorbed hydrogen and chemisorbed carbon monoxide.

props.name: Attempts to synthesise methanol from CO and H2 (1:2) at 1200-1500 lb/in2 over th
props.statement: Attempts to synthesise methanol from CO and H2 (1:2) at 1200-1500 lb/in2 over the catalyst most active for methanol decomposition failed, although equilibrium favours about 60-75 % conversion; only traces of methane and carbon dioxide were formed.

props.name: After methanol decomposition at 360 °C there is but little tendency to carbide f
props.statement: After methanol decomposition at 360 °C there is but little tendency to carbide formation, increasing slightly with catalyst activity; comparatively large amounts of CO and H2 are retained without reacting at 360 °C and are desorbed rather than reacting at 450 °C, so the X-CO complex is very stable.

props.name: The activity of a catalyst of this type also depends on the interval since its p
props.statement: The activity of a catalyst of this type also depends on the interval since its preparation; for maximum activity it must be prepared and reduced immediately before use.

props.name: Analysis of the gas during reduction of the 68.8 mol% Zn catalyst (H2 46 %, CO 8
props.statement: Analysis of the gas during reduction of the 68.8 mol% Zn catalyst (H2 46 %, CO 8 %, CO2 46 %, CH4 nil, N2-free) suggests reduction more probably by CO than by H2, but because of the water-gas reaction the results are indeterminate.

props.name: Reduction of the zinc oxide/chromium oxide catalysts by methanol is strongly exo
props.statement: Reduction of the zinc oxide/chromium oxide catalysts by methanol is strongly exothermic, its degree corresponding to the activity rather than the composition; the amount of reduction depends on chromium content. More active catalysts start reducing at lower temperature (68.8 mol% Zn about 250 °C; 18.8 mol% Zn about 280 °C).

props.name: The failure of the high-pressure syntheses is due to the catalyst being much mor
props.statement: The failure of the high-pressure syntheses is due to the catalyst being much more active for the decomposition of methanol and formaldehyde than for their synthesis (assumed more probable than inhibition by the metal of the reaction chamber).

props.name: The reactivating effect of overheating the catalyst is due to desorption of carb
props.statement: The reactivating effect of overheating the catalyst is due to desorption of carbon monoxide and hydrogen.

props.name: Methanol synthesis, parallel to the Craxford-Rideal Fischer-Tropsch mechanism, p
props.statement: Methanol synthesis, parallel to the Craxford-Rideal Fischer-Tropsch mechanism, proceeds by chemisorption of CO and of H on the catalyst X and reaction of chemisorbed CO with molecular hydrogen: X-CO + H2 -> X + CH3OH; chemisorbed CO with chemisorbed hydrogen gives side reactions (methane, formaldehyde).

Cryder and Frolich method: zinc hydroxide slurry evaporated with chromic acid
props.method: precipitation of zinc hydroxide from zinc nitrate with ammonia, addition of solid chromic acid to the slurry, evaporation to dryness, screening and drying
props.note: Catalysts with a high proportion of chromium were deliquescent.
steps: a concentrated solution of zinc nitrate prepared by dissolving chemically pure zinc oxide in nitric acid (printed '5 0 nitric acid')
solution heated to about 80 °C and concentrated ammonia solution added with constant stirring till free from acid
precipitate washed with water at about 80 °C (3 washings of 1 litre each)
slurry analysed for zinc; about 500 cc weighed out and the calculated quantity of solid chromic acid added
mixture evaporated to dryness with continual stirring, final stages on a water-bath
mass broken up, screened between 10 and 40 mesh (I.M.M.) and dried in an air oven at 110 °C for two hours

temperature.as_reported: dried in an air oven at 110°C. for two hours
